svg.text: Lattices attached to a prime-field ECDLP instance (E/F_p, P, Q = [k]P, prime order N)
Green: a lattice one can write down from public data. Amber: writable only with extra input (a lift or an oracle). Red: its basis or coordinates are the discrete log.
Exponents are of p. Every statement is derived or cited (RESEARCH_LATTICE_ECDLP_ROUTES.md §4–§6); none is measured here.
Public data
E: y² = x³ + ax + b over F_p
P, Q = [k]P, N = ord(P) prime
π (Frobenius); End(E) = R, Z-rank 2
λ: eigenvalue of an automorphism
Shoup: no generic method below √N
Writable without k
GLV / automorphism lattice {(a,b) : a + bλ ≡ 0 mod N}
dim 2, det N, λ₁ ≈ √N. Reduction gives the scalar split
k = k₁ + k₂λ and folds rho by √#Aut(E) ≤ √6 (ordinary E).
Constant factor only. Nothing in it depends on k.
Z[τ]-net zero lattice {(α,β) in Z[τ]² : α + kβ ≡ 0 mod π}
Z-rank 4, index N; a vector with N(α), N(β) well below √N exists, but
finding it is a two-dimensional baby-step giant-step: Θ(√N).
Closure §4.2, RESEARCH_NZMS_AMS_AUSTMS_2024_IDEAS.md (derived).
Coppersmith lattice for S_(m+1)(x₁,…,x_m, x(R)) ≡ 0 mod p
Factor base {x(P) < B}, B = p^β. Lattice root region ∏Xᵢ ≤ p^θ
with θ_m = 2 / ((m+1)·2^(m−1)) (box polytope, basic strategy).
Relation collection ≥ p^(1 − (m−1)θ_m/m): p^(5/6) at m = 2,
rising towards p^1. Rho parity needs θ ≥ m/(2(m−1)) ≥ 1/2.
Derived in §6; never met. The toy falsifier of §7 would measure θ₂.
Mordell–Weil lattice of a lift Ẽ/Q (or over F_p(t))
E(Q)/torsion with the Néron–Tate height is Euclidean; a relation
among lifted points solves the instance. JKSST 2000: an absolute
bound on relation coefficients kills dependence as p grows.
Refuted (xedni). Repo function-field line: toy only, p ≤ 31 (KN-FIND-003…011).
HNP / EC-HNP lattice (Boneh–Venkatesan; BHH 2001; Shani 2017)
Linear equations over Z/N from an oracle on bits of nonces or of
x([ab]P). LLL/BKZ recovers k from a few leaked bits per sample.
Needs representation-level leakage; a generic group has none.
Measured here: hnp_ecdsa.rs, multi_key_hnp.rs, GLV-HNP at 12/17/20 bits.
Basis or coordinates ⇔ the discrete log
Relation lattice L_k = {(a,b) in Z² : aP + bQ = O} = Z(N,0) + Z(−k,1)
det N, λ₁ ≈ √N. Any vector with b ≠ 0 gives k = −a/b mod N. Rho is a sampler
of L_k: a collision aP + bQ = a'P + b'Q is one vector, found in Θ(√N).
Without a vector there is no basis, so there is nothing to reduce.
Elementary; the r-dimensional form is KN-FIND-009's derivation 2.
Witness lattice W_r(k) in Z^(2r): {(c,d) : Σcᵢλᵢ + k·Σdᵢλᵢ ≡ 0 mod N}
Writing any basis is polynomial-time equivalent to solving the instance, and
needs no LLL: the one-dimensional nullspace mod N reads k off. Vieta supplies
∞-norm-1 vectors with d = 0: true relations that carry no logarithm.
crypto-autoresearcher knowledge/findings/KN-FIND-009.md (certificate + derivation).
Lenstra coordinates: E(F_p) is isomorphic to R/(π−1)R as an R-module, R of rank 2
The group is a quotient of a rank-2 lattice by an index-N sublattice. The map
is α -> α(P₀); inverting it on P means finding a + bπ with (a + bπ)P₀ = P, a
two-dimensional DLP (Gaudry–Schost): Θ(√N). Ordinary E has no larger End-module.
Lenstra, J. Number Theory 56 (1996), Theorem 1(a); read from the PDF.
Weil-restriction subspace: the linear object that works over F_(p^n)
Factor base = an F_p-subspace V of F_(p^n); Gaudry–Diem decomposition by Gröbner
bases, exponent 2(n−1)/n² in the group size. Over F_p itself the only F_p-subspaces
are 0 and F_p: there is no room, which is why no prime-field analogue exists.
Gaudry 2009; Diem 2011; Galbraith–Gaudry 2016 survey (read from HAL).
writing these down needs k, or a √N computation
Reading
writable; constant factor or √N
writable with a lift or an oracle
basis ⇔ solving the DLP
needs the log, a lift or an oracle
Derived or cited; none measured.
